evidence: The duplication is real, but the block sits between `<!-- BEGIN LIT INTEGRATION -->` markers, and the agent reports that `lit quickstart --refresh` reproduces both copies byte-for-byte. The single source is therefore lit's template. A hand edit to one copy would add a second writer, not remove one, so the reviewer's 'silently leaves the other stale' scenario does not happen.

The sentence does say 'no need to check in before running it', but it is lit's generated text and the next refresh would overwrite a local edit. `lit quickstart` is read-only, and the agent's permission mode still decides whether any command runs, so the security framing is overstated. The packet does not show whether the agent filed the wording concern against lit's template.
guidance_note: When declining a finding on generated text because 'the change belongs in the generator', file the ticket against the generator in the same reply so the concern is routed rather than dropped.

narrative: One review round raised two findings, and both were on lit's generated integration block in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. The agent pushed back on both because the text is generator output that `lit quickstart --refresh` reproduces exactly, and it merged two minutes later. Both pushbacks hold up: hand-editing the rendered output would be overwritten and would create a second writer.
guidance_observations: The reviewer has no way to tell generated blocks from hand-written ones, so marker-delimited generated regions keep drawing one-source-of-truth and wording findings that can only be answered upstream.

evidence: The diff adds `"postinstall": "patch-package"` but lists `patch-package` only in devDependencies. A production or nested install therefore has no binary for postinstall to run. The agent moved it to dependencies in ac82bc0.
guidance_note: When adding a postinstall patch-package step, check the full set before pushing: the runtime dependency, `patches` in `files`, and an exact pin on the patched package.

evidence: The patch file is named for ink@5.2.1 while package.json still says `ink: ^5.2.0`. A later 5.x could fail to apply the patch, or apply it to code it was never checked against. The agent pinned ink to exactly 5.2.1 in ac82bc0.
guidance_note: A patch file named for an exact version must ship in the same commit as an exact pin of that dependency.

evidence: The CLAUDE.md pointer `stylesheet.ts:2008` was stale at the reviewed head. The agent fixed it from a grep of the file (`2000:export function resolveStylesForWidget`) and did not copy the reviewer's computed 2020, which the agent's own later deletions had made wrong.
guidance_note: Docs that point at a file:line in a file the same PR edits should cite the symbol name, or be re-grepped after the last edit, because line numbers drift with every fix.

evidence: The existing reversed-cell test checked only the edge colour and the `7` SGR. The agent confirmed that swapping roles 2 and 3 left every test green. It then added background-SGR assertions for both roles, derived from Textual's `get_box`, and showed the new test fails when the roles are swapped.
guidance_note: When adding a lookup table that maps enumerated roles to behaviour, write a test that tells each pair of entries apart, then swap two entries to confirm the test fails.

evidence: `"files": ["dist"]` leaves `patches/` out of the published tarball. In that case patch-package exits 0 with 'No patch files found', so consumers silently lose the fix. The agent added `patches` to `files` in ac82bc0.
guidance_note: When a postinstall script reads repo files, check that the `files` array ships them; `npm pack --dry-run` lists what a consumer actually gets.

evidence: The crash on partial-alpha backgrounds is real. The agent's table shows `background: blue 50%` already throws at master 433dc97, where `edgeBoxProps` does not exist, so the PR did not introduce it and the reviewer's traced route is not the mechanism. The agent fixed the producer instead of the call-site guard the reviewer proposed: `colorToInkValue` now returns undefined for alpha 0 and opaque hex6 otherwise. That closes F6 and F7 together and removes the `is_transparent` special case.
guidance_note: When a fix special-cases one bad value from a producer (`is_transparent`), enumerate the producer's whole output range first; here that means every alpha below 1, not just 0.

evidence: The agent reproduced both of the reviewer's examples (`#ff000080`, `transparent`): each renders at master and throws at 9502fc2, because the edge colour moved from chalk to rich-js's stricter parser. The agent fixed the producer rather than adding a guard in `edgesOf`, which is the better cure. Reply 2 corrects an incorrect causal claim the agent had made earlier in reply 1.
guidance_note: When rerouting a value to a stricter consumer (chalk to rich-js), check every spelling the producer can emit against the new consumer's parser before pushing.

evidence: The hunk shows `edgeBoxProps` called unconditionally for both border and outline, and the old code did no work when no border was declared, so the cost regression was real. The agent memoised `paintCell` with a bounded cache instead of adding the reviewer's skip branch, kept one code path, and measured 48.7µs to 13.0µs with no border.
guidance_note: When a change makes per-widget work unconditional on a full-tree recascade path, measure it before pushing and cache any pure render step.

narrative: One review round raised eight findings against the original PR, and none was caused by a fix. Three were packaging gaps from adding a postinstall patch-package step, two were rgba crashes from routing colours through rich-js, and the rest were a perf cost, a missing test and a stale line pointer. The agent accepted every premise but corrected F6's attribution: the crash existed at master. It fixed both crashes once at the producer and handled the perf finding with memoisation. The PR is still open with no second review round in the packet, so whether the fixes caused new findings is not shown.
guidance_observations: Three of the eight findings were one checklist (dependency placement, `files`, exact pin) for vendoring a patch; a pre-push check for postinstall patches would have avoided all three.
The agent checked its own causal claims against master and the pre-fix commit, which caught the reviewer's wrong attribution in F6 and the agent's own wrong prerequisite claim in F7.

evidence: The finding names npm commands still present in visual-tests/README.md, visual-tests/Dockerfile and spec/impl/phase-*.md after `packageManager` was pinned to pnpm. The thread has no reply, but the agent's issue comment says those files now use pnpm, and round 1 on 3d02635 shows 8 spec/impl and 3 visual-tests files changed.
guidance_note: When switching package managers, grep the whole repo for `npm run`, `npm install` and `npm test` (docs, Dockerfiles, specs) before opening the PR, not just the README and scripts.

narrative: The pnpm migration converted the root README and scripts but left npm commands in visual-tests docs, the Dockerfile and the phase specs. The single finding asked for the rest of the sweep. The agent completed it, answering in an issue comment rather than on the thread, and round 1 approved. Round 1 was the re-review of the completed original migration, not a fix-caused round.
guidance_observations: The agent replied in an issue comment and left the finding thread without a reply, so the thread-level record shows no response even though the fix landed.
